title: Tiered administration
subtitle: Admin seats, the tier rules & where privilege may sign in
description: Build the administration plane before the fleet: three administration seats on two machines in VLAN 60 (the endpoint seat runs as a virtual machine on the server seat), directory-enforced tier restrictions proven by both successful in-tier sessions and logged out-of-tier denials, and the move of earlier console work — SBD-DHCP01's administration and the assessment tools — onto the seats.
outcomes: Stand up single-purpose administration seats for each tier in the Admin OU, with the endpoint seat a virtual machine on the server seat.
Enforce and prove per-tier sign-in restrictions with captured denial evidence.
Move SBD-DHCP01's administration and the assessment tools onto the seats, each tier on its own.

stages.title: Design the tiers and the admin seats
stages.detail: Tiering is one sentence with teeth: credentials that control a tier never touch a less-trusted one. Write that policy against the OU structure and give each tier its seat and its group — all before any host is built.

stages.title: Build the administration systems
stages.detail: Privileged work gets dedicated, hardened seats: a Tier 0 jump host that runs no virtual machines, and a server-administration seat that also runs the endpoint seat as a virtual machine. Each seat sits in the Admin OU, does nothing but administer, and is maintained by its own group.

stages.title: Restrict where privilege can sign in
stages.detail: The tier rule becomes real when the directory refuses the wrong sign-in. Give Tier 0 servers their own OU first, deny privileged logons on lower tiers by policy, protect the highest accounts, and make the refusal something you can show in a log.

stages.title: Prove the tiers end to end
stages.detail: Run the matrix: every tier's administration works from its seat, every cross-tier attempt fails with an event, and course 1.7's addressing service still behaves exactly as registered.

stages.title: Move the scan tools, rescan, and hand off
stages.detail: Three new seats joined, SBD-DHCP01 changed hands, and the directory's logon policy changed — the cadence fires again. Move the assessment tools off the domain controllers onto the seats, baseline the physical seats, rescan what changed, and hand the next course a network administered only from somewhere safe.

outcomeSummary: Privileged sessions that only ever start from the right seat.
